hooks.text: Pluto has not finished a single orbit since its discovery.
It takes Pluto 248 years to make one trip around the Sun.
Pluto was demoted before it could finish even one orbit as a planet.

title: Why Pluto Never Finished Its Orbit
description: Pluto was a planet for 76 years, but it has not even completed one trip around the Sun since its discovery in 1930.

beats.text: Pluto has not finished a single orbit since its discovery.
beats.visual: High-resolution portrait of Pluto featuring Tombaugh Regio from New Horizons, 2015

beats.text: In February 1930, Clyde Tombaugh used a blink comparator to find the icy world at Lowell Observatory.
beats.visual: Black and white photograph of Clyde Tombaugh with the blink comparator at Lowell Observatory, 1930

beats.text: Most people believe Pluto was a major planet for 76 years before its demotion.
beats.visual: The original 1930 discovery plates of Pluto showing a tiny moving speck

beats.text: But this icy world is actually smaller than seven solar system moons, including Earth's Moon.
beats.visual: Infographic comparing the size of Pluto to Earth's Moon and Ganymede

beats.text: The International Astronomical Union demoted it in 2006 for failing to clear its orbital neighborhood.
beats.visual: Wide shot of astronomers voting at the 2006 IAU General Assembly in Prague

beats.text: Pluto's path is so extreme that between 1979 and 1999, it was closer to the Sun than Neptune.
beats.visual: Diagram of the solar system showing Pluto's elliptical orbit crossing inside Neptune's orbit

beats.text: A single trip around the Sun takes this world roughly 248 Earth years.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the distant Sun as seen from the surface of Pluto

beats.text: Pluto will finally finish that journey in the year 2178.
beats.visual: Backlit view of Pluto's blue atmospheric haze layers from New Horizons, 2015
queries: Pluto atmosphere blue haze New Horizons

better_than_last: Formulated the final beat as a complete, non-dangling sentence that seamlessly loops back to the hook.
